newsitem.title: UK: General Cable sees no takeover in short-term.
newsitem.headline: General Cable sees no takeover in short-term.

text.p: UK cable TV and telecoms group General Cable said on Thursday that it saw no advantage in merging with another company or being taken over in the short-term but was keeping its options open.
"In a room full of marriageable people, we are a very pretty girl," finance director David Miller told a news conference.

Amid speculation that the group has held takeover talks with rivals such as cable operator Telewest Communications Plc or Comcast UK Cable Partners Ltd as consolidations sweeps the industry, the company said its role was to maximise shareholder value.
But it noted that in the short-term, this just meant running the business effectively.
"We are constantly talking to our partners in other franchises," noted chairman Sir Anthony Cleaver. "At the moment, we do not see any advantage in a (strategic) divergence."
But he said the group would continue to talk to others in the industry "because one never knows what is going to happen".
Last year, Cable and Wireless Plc announced that its UK unit Mercury was merging with three other cable companies to create Cable and Wireless Communications -- Britain's biggest cable group.
